title: Generate–Verify–Repair Pipeline Efficacy for LLM-Generated Network Configurations (Repaired Preregistration)
research_question: Does an iterative generate–verify–repair pipeline that pairs hosted-LLM generation with deterministic verification and deterministic repair heuristics (bounded ≤3 iterations) yield a higher emulator-executable configuration success rate than ungated LLM generation?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: The generate–verify–repair pipeline (guarded) has a higher emulator-executable success proportion than ungated LLM outputs (paired estimand: guarded minus baseline).

H2: Most remaining emulator execution failures after deterministic repair will be attributable to emulator-modeled runtime/state interactions (timing/BGP convergence) rather than purely syntactic or trivially fixable logical errors.
H3: ≤3 deterministic repair iterations capture the majority of verifier-detected, syntactic/structural faults; marginal yield is small after iteration 3.
exploratory_questions: EQ1: What automated failure-taxonomy labels (syntactic, verifier-failure, runtime/convergence, ACL-mismatch, ambiguous) dominate uncorrected cases?
EQ2: How often deterministic repairs introduce config-line churn (lines changed) even when they enable emulator success?
benchmark_scope: Synthetic NetOps intent corpus (n=200 confirmatory intents) covering single-device and small multi-device changes (ACLs, route addition/removal, interface config).
Dockerized emulator images (Mininet + FRR + standard Linux router toolchain) and deterministic verifier (NetKAT/MEV-style verifier) run locally in Docker.
model_scope: Hosted LLM for generation (hosted_model_api_available). Exact provider/model identifier will be recorded and hashed at execution time in the artifact release.

No human-in-the-loop; deterministic repair heuristics (rule-based, grammar-driven) implement repairs in the recommended scenario. Optional high-budget scenario allows secondary hosted-LLM guided repairs (preregistered if used).
transformation_scope: Config normalization (whitespace/ordering canonicalization), CLI tokenization, verifier-translation mapping, deterministic repair heuristics (pattern-based fixes), automated failure-labeling pipeline.
secondary_estimands: proportion of verifier-detected faults corrected by repairs
distribution of automated failure-taxonomy labels among uncorrected failures
sampling_plan: Confirmatory set: n=200 natural-language change intents curated to span single-device and small cross-device changes. Each intent is executed in paired fashion: (A) ungated LLM generation (baseline) and (B) guarded generate–verify–repair pipeline. For each intent both arms must attempt to produce a final configuration; if an arm fails to produce any syntactically-parseable configuration due to provider/API failure, that arm is treated as a failure (see missingness_plan). An optional discovery set of 50 additional intents will be used for exploratory analyses and tooling validation but not included in the confirmatory paired estimator.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis executed by available_analysis_contract paired_binary_analysis_v1 computing the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (primary estimand). Primary hypothesis test: McNemar test for paired binary success/failure (two-sided α=0.05). Report absolute and relative risk differences with 95% CIs. Secondary analyses: logistic regression (emulator success ~ initial_verifier_fail + devices_touched + repair_iterations + config_lines) reported as ORs with 95% CIs. Report repair-iteration yield curve and automated failure-taxonomy counts. All analysis code and seeds recorded; deterministic analysis executor and result schema paired_binary_episode_v1 used.
multiplicity_plan: Single predeclared primary estimand (paired success-rate difference). Secondary estimands reported descriptively and explicitly labeled exploratory. No multiplicity adjustment for exploratory outcomes; primary test alone controls pre-specified α. Any additional hypothesis tests introduced post-hoc will be clearly labeled exploratory.
missingness_plan: If hosted-LLM/API provider errors or timeouts prevent producing an output for an arm of a pair, treat that arm as a failure (binary=0) in the primary analysis (complete-pair-with-failure-as-zero sensitivity). Report counts and perform sensitivity analysis excluding pairs with provider errors. All provider/API failures, timeouts, and retry attempts are logged; retry policy: single automatic retry for transient HTTP/timeout errors within a 60s backoff window, otherwise record as provider failure.

risk_factors: Re-use of pre-lock development artifacts (prompts, example configs) contaminating the confirmatory corpus.
Leakage of solution seeds (hashed prompts/config templates) into the intent corpus.
detection_procedures: Artifact-hash comparison: compute SHA-256 hashes of all prompt templates, intent texts, and generated artifacts and compare against a pre-lock artifact hash list (pre-lock hashes are recorded in the execution manifest).
Timestamp and provenance checks for all artifacts stored in the artifact repository; automated detection of any artifact whose creation timestamp precedes the autonomy-lock marker.
Automated duplicate-text detector (exact and near-duplicate via Jaccard on token shingles) to flag intents or outputs matching pre-lock corpus.
item_flagging_rules: Flag any intent / generated artifact whose SHA-256 matches a pre-lock hash OR whose near-duplicate score with any pre-lock artifact > 0.9.
Flag any artifact with creation timestamp earlier than autonomy-lock marker.
Automatically exclude flagged items from confirmatory analysis and report them in a contamination log.
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Flagged items are excluded from confirmatory paired analysis; primary analysis is run on the remaining confirmed-clean n. Sensitivity analysis reports results including flagged items (labelled). All flags and exclusions are recorded and published in the artifact release.
residual_uncertainty: Undetected pre-lock similarities below the near-duplicate threshold remain possible.
External data leaked into hosted-model provider prompts or completions cannot be fully controlled; this is reported as residual uncertainty.

budget_scenarios.description: Deterministic-repair-first (recommended) — use hosted LLM only for generation; repairs implemented as deterministic rule-based heuristics (no additional hosted-LLM repair calls).
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Per-intent model calls = 1 (baseline ungated generation) + 1 (pipeline initial generation) = 2 calls/intent. 200 intents × 2 = 400 model calls. Verifier and repairs are deterministic CPU-run Docker components (NetKAT/MEV-style verifier and rule-based repair scripts). Docker and CPU resources available per capability manifest.

budget_scenarios.description: LLM-assisted repairs enabled (high-budget) — allow up to 3 hosted-LLM repair iterations per pipeline intent using secondary hosted LLM for repair guidance; baseline still uses one hosted call.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Worst-case per-intent calls: baseline=1 + pipeline initial=1 + up to 3 repair LLM calls = 5 calls/intent. 200 intents × 5 = 1000 model calls (worst-case budget). Expected average repair iterations ~1 yields ~600 expected calls but preregister worst-case cap. Hosted-model API availability is confirmed in capability manifest; total planned calls are within the manifest limit (≤10000).

power_plan.target_effect: Absolute increase of 0.15 (15 percentage points) in emulator-executable success rate for guarded vs baseline
power_plan.clustering_unit: intent (paired design: same intent across both arms)
power_plan.calculation_method: Approximate paired-power (McNemar/paired-proportion) calculation under simple assumptions: baseline success p0≈0.50, guarded success p1≈0.65 (absolute diff 0.15), two-sided α=0.05. Using standard approximations for paired binary tests, n=200 yields power >80% to detect a 15 pp paired improvement (conservative estimate).
assumptions: Baseline ungated emulator success rate ≈ 50% (domain-informed prior).
Conservative within-intent independence assumption for power approximation.
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With n=200 paired intents, the minimum detectable absolute paired difference at 80% power is approximately 10–15 percentage points depending on discordant pair rates; sensitivity analyses will report exact detectable MDE curves.
sensitivity_analyses: Recompute paired power and detectable effect assuming baseline p0 in {0.3, 0.5, 0.7}.
Perform sensitivity where provider/API failures are treated as missing (complete-case) vs treated as failure (primary).

transformation_families: cli_tokenizer_v1 (deterministic CLI tokenization for verifier translation)
llm_guided_repair_v1 (only in high-budget scenario; preregistered prompt templates and hash)
semantic_equivalence_checks: Round-trip verifier check: normalize → verifier-translate → verifier input; ensure the verifier input maps back to the normalized config (deterministic mapping).

Automated diff invariants: ensure that deterministic normalization does not remove semantic statements (e.g., ACL entries) by cross-checking presence/absence of policy statements pre/post transformation.
automatic_rejection_rules: Reject any generated config failing syntactic parse by the canonical CLI parser (deterministic parser returns parse errors).
Reject any config where canonicalization drops statements required by the intent (automated check comparing extracted intent predicates).
Reject outputs containing blacklisted constructs (per safety rules) detected via deterministic regex filters.
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Automated deterministic replay audit on 10% random sample of confirmatory intents: reproduce generation + normalization + verification + repair deterministically and compute hash of final artifact; any mismatch triggers automated re-execution for that intent (up to 2 auto-retries). All audits logged and published.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: Provide a deterministic mapping table from canonical CLI tokens to verifier predicates; validate mapping with unit tests (100% pass required) before experiment execution.
residual_risks: Normalization heuristics may under-approximate vendor-specific CLI idiosyncrasies.
LLM-guided repairs (in high-budget) may still produce plausible but semantically incorrect edits; we mitigate by preferring deterministic repairs in recommended scenario.

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: Emulator fidelity vs vendor production devices for some runtime behaviours (BGP timer interactions, proprietary vendor-side state) — experiments are explicitly bounded to the dockerized Mininet+FRR emulator and deterministic verifier; external generalization is a limitation.

Using hosted LLM generation implies nondeterminism across provider model versions; exact model identifier will be recorded at runtime and hashed, but provider-side nondeterminism (model updates) remains a residual uncertainty.

Confirmation bias risk when deterministic repairs cannot correct deeper semantic errors that would benefit from diverse repair strategies — mitigated by preferring deterministic repairs and optionally enabling LLM-guided repair only in secondary scenario with full artifact recording.
